name: Willis Towers Watson plc (WTW)

corporate_actions.event: Sold TRANZACT (direct-to-consumer Medicare marketplace); reported revenue -2% in 2025 reflects divestiture

Re-entering reinsurance broking via Willis Re joint venture with Bain Capital; JV to acquire BMS Re's US reinsurance broking business (expected close Q4-26); Neil Eckert appointed JV CEO from early 2027
Acquired Newfront (US) and Cushon (UK workplace savings) - integrations 'on track'

geography.fx_notes: Irish domicile, London HQ; material GBP/EUR revenue and costs. Exact 10-K split not extracted in this pass. Career business exposed to Middle East.

kpis.name: Q3-26 organic: Risk & Broking / Health, Wealth & Career

company_fcf.definition: Company FCF = cash from operations less capex

acquisitions.notes: Newfront, Cushon; Willis Re/Bain JV with BMS Re US acquisition; amounts not extracted

management.senior_turnover_5y: High after failed Aon merger (2021): sale of Willis Re to Gallagher, executive departures; stabilised since (not quantified)
management.guidance_record: Transformation program completed; margin expansion delivered 2024-25; ~100bp FY26 expansion reaffirmed

guidance.value: ~30% enterprise target by 2028 (per transcript summary; not re-verified)

evidence: Broking and benefits consulting largely renewing (S1)
BD&O -2% on implementation delays shows some project timing risk (S2)
A.rationale: Mostly recurring with some project/consulting timing.

evidence: Exited reinsurance broking 2021, now rebuilding via JV (S2)
B.rationale: Strong in specialty and HWC, but weaker reinsurance franchise than MMC/Aon.

evidence: Adj op margin 25.2% vs higher at peers (S3)
C.rationale: Scale present but margins lag top peers; improving.

D.rationale: Moderate runway; re-entry into reinsurance adds optionality.

evidence: London HQ, Irish domicile, global operations (S1)
E.rationale: Balanced NA/Europe spread; split not extracted.

evidence: Post-2021 disruption and re-entry into reinsurance (S2)
F.rationale: Mixed: recent delivery good, strategy volatile.

evidence: Reinsurance exit 2021 then re-entry via JV 2026 (S2)
G.rationale: Buybacks sensible; strategic reversals cost value.

I1.rationale: Benefits admin and actuarial consulting more automatable than large-risk broking (INFERENCE).

evidence: Propel AI/automation programme drives margin plan (S2)

ai.notes: Propel AI programme for internal productivity.

sector_specific.organic_ex_rate_note: INFERENCE: R&B +5% in Q3-26 amid declining property rates; NA growth double-digit in construction/surety/transactional; rate contribution judged ~0-1pt in 2026.

gates.notes: G1: ~2.6x gross debt/EBITDA (PitchBook). FCF $1.55bn vs NI $1.6bn 2025 -> ~95% conversion (company FCF / PitchBook NI). No pending takeover.

bull_points: Margin catch-up story: +130bp 2025, +~100bp 2026, 30% target, with FCF rising faster than revenue.
Large buybacks (~$1bn+/yr) at a lower multiple than MMC/AON (INFERENCE).
Reinsurance re-entry via capital-light JV adds growth optionality.
bear_points: Lowest organic growth of the global three (4% Q3-26).
HWC exposed to benefits-admin automation and Middle East disruption; BD&O implementation delays.
Strategic stop-start (Willis Re sold 2021, re-entered 2026) raises execution risk.
thesis_breakers: Organic growth < 3% for a full year.
Adjusted operating margin fails to expand in 2027.
